AUTHOR: Jenrette
TITLE: Shark detection and classification with machine learning
REGION: Global (sharkPulse / Instagram images; BRUV and YouTube videos of varying habitats)
SPECIES: Sharks: 74 genera / 219 species in training data; classifier covers 26 genera + 47 species (e.g., Carcharodon carcharias, Prionace glauca, Rhincodon typus, Orectolobus spp., Sphyrna spp., Carcharhinus spp.)
DATA: sharkPulse crowd-sourced archive + Instagram: 53,345 shark images (24,546 originals + SL crops) and 50,260 non-shark images; test media: 2 BRUV videos + 5 YouTube videos (136 min, 8,185 frames), 14 Instagram hashtag sets, 400 new Instagram images
D2: 90/10 train/validation on images (SI); SC split not specified; separate test media (videos, Instagram)
D_EV: Sec. 2.2: 'We trained the model with 90% of the training set, and validated with the remaining images'; Sec. 2.4: 'We removed duplicate images by comparing their pixel content and retaining only one copy'
R_EV: Sec. 2.4: 'we applied the SD to three common cases of data generation methods involving sharks' (BRUV + YouTube videos, Instagram); Sec. 3: 'Accuracy for all models across the three data-generation methods are shown in Figure 4e'
C_EV: Sec. 2.4: 'The SL threshold was increased to 0.99 to minimize the false-positive rate'; Sec. 3.2: 'We spent 6.2 hours manually validating all of the extracted frames (n = 8,185 frames)' ... 'false-positive rate of 7%'; Fig. 3 ROC over thresholds 5e-6 to 0.999
E_EV: Sec. 2.4: 'we calculated recall, precision, specificity and F1' and 'false-positive rate (FPR) and false-negative rate (FNR)'; no abundance/occurrence variable quantified against a reference
ARCH: Shark Locator: Faster R-CNN (TensorFlow Model Garden, COCO-trained); Shark Identifier: VGG16 (ImageNet) binary; Shark Classifier: DenseNet201 hierarchical genus -> species models
METR: Recall (top-1, top-3), precision, specificity, F1, FPR, FNR, ROC AUC, accuracy
NOTE: Text file is the author manuscript (Nov 2021) of the Ecological Informatics paper. Mixed-media study: training images are mostly above/below-water web photos, test includes BRUV footage; underwater component is partial. Shark Locator was trained only on COCO (236 shark images), not fine-tuned. D3 = Y refers to exact-duplicate removal (pixel comparison) applied to Instagram test sets, not near-duplicate/frame clustering of training data; D1 is image-level random 90/10 for the SI, and the SC split is not described. R3 interpreted as external-vs-internal performance reported (Fig. 4e across three data-generation methods); verifier may downgrade to P. C5 based on manual validation of all 8,185 extracted frames with FPR 7% for a no-shark video. E_ALL = N although the paper's aim is occurrence records; no ecological quantity is computed in this paper. DSHR = 공개 ('We provide these models and their training data in an instructional GitHub repository').
